report.root_cause: The StatsCache plugin's config (plugins/StatsCache/config.yml) was changed to retain-history: true and hot-reloaded at 07:33:51. The plugin then kept a history cache in memory that grew by about 290 KB per entry (818 entries / ~234 MB, then 920 entries / ~263 MB). Heap went from ~350 MB to ~627 of 768 MB, heading for an out-of-memory crash.
report.actions: 1) Watched status and saw heap climbing (348 -> 390 -> 404 -> 535 MB). 2) Read the logs and found StatsCache config reloaded with retain-history=true at 07:33:51. 3) Declared the incident. 4) Read plugins/StatsCache/config.yml and ran 'statscache stats': 818 entries, ~234 MB held. 5) Edited plugins/StatsCache/config.yml to set retain-history: false (left history-size: 1000 unchanged). The plugin hot-reloaded it at 07:34:37 (retain-history=false). 6) Ran 'statscache flush', which freed 920 entries (~263 MB). 7) Checked the result: heap went down to ~301 MB, StatsCache stayed at 0 entries, and heap now follows the normal garbage-collection cycle (rose to ~450 MB, then fell to ~317 MB). TPS stayed at 20 the whole time. No restart, no bans, no deletions.
report.residual_risk: I don't know who turned on retain-history or why. If it is turned on again, the leak comes back. history-size: 1000 does not limit memory safely, because 1000 entries at ~290 KB each is ~290 MB on a 768 MB heap. The plugin owner should either cap memory for the history or keep retain-history off. The in-memory stats history was flushed and can't be recovered (stats.json is still there).
